node-1.label: A 53-year-old woman has had a lump on the posterior aspect of the right knee joint for 3 years, with pain and discomfort when walking or standing with the knee extended

node-2.label: The patient is a 53-year-old woman with no underlying diseases and a 3-year history of a lump on the posterior aspect of the right knee joint

node-3.label: The lump is growing at the posterior aspect of the right knee joint and causes pain and discomfort during walking or standing with the knee joint extended

node-4.label: Physical examination: right knee range of motion 10-130°, no internal swelling of the knee joint, no tenderness of medial or lateral joint line, normal Lachman test, normal valgus and varus stress tests, and a 3×3 cm palpable lump at the posterior aspect of the right knee joint

why.why: MRI demonstrates a multi-lobulated 3.3 cm popliteal fossa cyst with normal intra-articular structures, directly consistent with a Baker's cyst. Chronic symptoms and normal joint examination further support this diagnosis. However, because joint communication is not documented, the key criterion to exclude soft tissue neoplasm is not met, so confidence is raised to 0.78 rather than higher.

MRI identifies a popliteal fossa cyst with imaging features consistent with a Baker's cyst, reducing the likelihood of soft tissue neoplasm. Nevertheless, absent documentation of joint communication prevents absolute exclusion of a soft tissue neoplasm, so it retains a low but non-negligible confidence of 0.18.

MRI shows normal intra-articular structures, adding imaging confirmation to the normal joint examination and negative stress tests. Intra-articular pathology is therefore even less likely and confidence is reduced to 0.05.

node-8.label: MRI shows a multi-lobulated 3.3 cm popliteal fossa cyst

node-9.label: MRI shows normal intra-articular structures of the knee

node-10.label: MRI does not document communication between the popliteal fossa cyst and the knee joint
